chosen.table: none: no numeric results table in paper
chosen.why_this_choice: Rule 3 requires a per-dataset table containing both the proposed method and SMOTE; the paper reports results only as four line plots (Fig. 2), each a different metric/classifier/dataset, plotted against over-sampling percent. No G-mean is reported. Values were not read off the plots to avoid estimating numbers.

win_claim.quote: The experiments show that the performance of Safe-Level-SMOTE evaluated by precision and F-value are better than that of SMOTE and Borderline-SMOTE when decision trees C4.5 are applied as classifiers.
win_claim.page: PDF p.7 (printed p.481, Section 5 Conclusion; page inferred from text extraction order)

notes: Only 2 UCI datasets (Table 3, printed p.480): Satimage (class 4 as minority; 6,435 instances, 37 attributes, 626 pos, 5,809 neg, 9.73% minority) and Haberman (306, 4, 81, 225, 26.47%). Metrics: precision, recall, F-value (beta=1), AUC; classifiers C4.5, Naive Bayes, SVMs; k=5; 10-fold CV. Results only in Fig. 2 (line plots over over-sampling percent; labels ORG, SMOTE, BORD, SAFE); each panel shows a single dataset/classifier/metric combination, so no metric/classifier is available for both datasets. AUC is only for Haberman with SVMs (Fig. 2d), where text says Safe-Level-SMOTE and SMOTE show similar AUC. Figures were not rendered/digitised; text extraction was clean. Page numbers: PDF pages 1-8 = printed pp. 475-482; Fig. 2 and the Conclusion appear on printed p.481 (inferred from text extraction order, not visually verified). Duplicate copy of this PDF also exists in the 'Both' folder.
